rounds.text: The most compelling argument for Maximus International Ltd lies in its phenomenal fundamental momentum, highlighted by a staggering 489% compounded profit growth over the trailing twelve months [E21] and a screen-reason pointing to a net profit increase of 1600% YoY [E64]. This explosive profit surge massively dwarfs the 5-year price growth of 6% [E22], directly signaling that fundamentals are outpacing the stock and that the business is starting to outperform expectations [E53, E54]. Adding to this strength, the company enjoys a perfect relative-strength rating of 100 against the Nifty 500 [E48], with the price trading above both its 50-day and 200-day moving averages in an established technical uptrend [E47]. Operations are also becoming significantly more efficient, evidenced by debtor days improving markedly from 169 down to 116 days [E56] alongside positive operating and free cash flows of Rs 2.08 Cr and Rs 0.50 Cr respectively in Mar 2026 [E34, E35]. Furthermore, capital expenditure is largely complete with Capital Work-in-Progress dropping to zero, implying new capacity is coming online [E39], all backed by a healthy, conservatively financed balance sheet carrying a low debt-to-equity ratio of 0.15x [E37] and a supportive sector tailwind score [E72]. Conceded: [E1], [E2], [E4], [E11], [E13], [E15], [E16], [E23], [E29], [E30], [E40], [E42], [E43], [E50], [E57], [E58], [E59], [E60], [E61], [E62], [E68], [E69].

Maximus International Ltd carries significant valuation and operational risks that are not supported by the underlying business fundamentals. The stock trades at an expensive P/E of 55.7x and a price-to-book ratio of 4.59x [E1, E2], while a discounted cash flow model values the intrinsic price at Rs 10 against a market price of Rs 13.5, leaving a negative margin of safety of -37.3% [E42, E43]. Furthermore, core operating performance shows severe deterioration, with annual operating margin dropping to -23% in March 2026—a 22 percentage point decline over three years—and quarterly operating margin collapsing to -166% [E29, E30]. Top-line expansion has stagnated badly, evidenced by a poor 3-year compounded sales growth of -33% and a 5-year growth rate of just 2% [E15, E16]. Compounded further, the company has a low 3-year median return on equity of 5% and exhibits negative earnings quality indicators, such as reported earnings including Rs 6.60 Cr of other income alongside a zero dividend yield [E27, E58, E61]. Finally, insider confidence is waning as promoter holding has steadily decreased by over five percentage points from September 2023 to June 2026 [E40]. Conceded: [E6].

Conceded: [E1], [E2], [E42], [E43], [E58], and [E61]. While the bear highlights rich headline multiples and a negative DCF margin of safety, these traditional models overlook explosive earnings velocity where compounded profit growth over the trailing twelve months reached an astonishing 489% alongside a 79% three-year profit growth rate [E20, E21]. Furthermore, the bear's focus on historical margin compression ignores the concrete operational recovery seen in improving debtor days from 169 to 116 days, positive operating cash flow of Rs 2.08 Cr, and positive free cash flow of Rs 0.50 Cr in March 2026 [E34, E35, E56]. The company operates with a conservatively financed debt-to-equity ratio of just 0.15x while completing its capital expenditure, as evidenced by CWIP dropping 100% to zero, positioning new capacity to come online [E37, E39]. This exceptional fundamental momentum is validated by the broader market, driving a relative-strength rating of 100 against the Nifty 500 and placing the stock firmly above its 50-day and 200-day moving averages [E47, E48]. Finally, the business benefits directly from a robust sector tailwind in Services, which holds a strong tailwind score of +0.58 and outperforms sector benchmarks on key ratios like price-to-earnings and price-to-book [E6, E7, E73].

Conceded: [E34], [E35], [E37], [E39], [E47], [E48], [E73]. While the bull points to explosive trailing profit growth and technical strength [E21, E48], the core valuation is inflated at a P/E of 55.7x and a price-to-book of 4.59x, leaving a negative DCF margin of safety of -37.3% [E1, E2, E43]. Furthermore, the reverse DCF indicates that today's price already demands an aggressive 22.3% earnings growth rate, surpassing the base case of 18.0% [E44]. The company's underlying top-line health remains weak, with a 3-year compounded sales growth of -33% and 5-year sales growth of just 2% [E15, E16]. Operational quality is also undermined by earnings quality concerns, specifically that earnings include Rs 6.60 Cr of other income, alongside a decade-long median ROE of just 4% [E25, E61]. Finally, insider alignment is deteriorating as promoter holdings have declined to 57.58% down from 62.65%, and the stock provides a 0.00% dividend yield despite reported profits [E4, E40, E58].
